stem:
Farhan has finished Koch Snowflake step $0$: one equilateral triangle. He applies the side-replacement rule once to get step $1$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Call the answer "equilateral triangle", without applying the side-replacement rule.
Update only one side, skipping that every current side gets the same replacement.
Replace every current side: divide into $3$ equal parts, raise an equilateral bump on the middle third and remove that middle segment, so all $3$ sides are updated.
Say the jagged snowflake boundary is what produces the replacement rule.

teacher.key_rationale: Each step replaces every current side by the same bump rule. Relabelling without replacing, updating only one side, or reversing the jagged boundary into the rule all miss that full-boundary replacement.
